signal: Stampli raised a $61M Blackstone-led Series D and launched Stampli Procurement plus Stampli Edge for SMBs.

email.body1:
Blake, saw Stampli closed a $61M Series D and rolled out Procurement and the new Edge product for SMBs.

New products mean a bigger target list, and that floods the SDR team with more accounts than reps can follow up on while ramping, so speed-to-lead slips. Our AI SDR handles research, writing, and follow-up autonomously, so reps stay in conversations: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I had our AI SDR draft three personalized emails to three of Stampli's top target accounts. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through them?
email.subject2: your outbound, 3 things I would change
email.body2:
Blake, quick follow-up for Stampli.

With two new products to seed, the bottleneck is rarely the messaging, it is follow-up volume and response speed across a team still learning the new motions. That is exactly where reply rate quietly leaks.

Worth 15 minutes? I will walk you through a teardown of Stampli's current outbound, three things I would change. Our best-practice patterns alone usually lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Blake, last bit of proof for Stampli.

Memgraph had more accounts in play than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Stampli's reply rate likely compares to other late-stage startups. Want to grab time so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Blake, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If cutting follow-up load and ramp time is not a priority for the team this quarter, no problem at all. Launching two products at once keeps an SDR org plenty busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your SDR motion? I will tailor it to Stampli either way.
